Soft Execution Continued in FY26; FY27 Growth Banks on Strong OB: 
Revenue/EBITDA fell to ~Rs70.1/7.3bn in FY26 due to (a) compressed OB 
in the beginning of the fiscal; and (b) recent added orders, which are yet to enter 
execution. Looking ahead, the management has guided the revenue to grow by 
~30-40% in FY27 with ~150-200bps expansion in EBITDA margin, as the 
company witnessed a record order inflow of ~Rs 185bn, whi ch is guided at 
~Rs100-120bn in FY27.  
Annuity Business : Coal MDO achieved ~29mmt (vs. original target of 
23mmt), which is expected to touch ~37/47/57mmt in FY27/28/29e. Recently 
added bauxite MDO is expected to begin operations in the next three years.

FY27/28/29e. Recently 
added bauxite MDO is expected to begin operations in the next three years. 
MDO revenue was ~Rs16.9bn in FY27 (vs, ~Rs16.1bn in FY25). EBITDA 
margin contracted from ~26% to ~23% due to slow evacuation by the client 
and rise in HSD cost, which is expected to normalise, going forward. 
InvIT: The company plans to monetise eleven assets in two tranches in 
1QFY27 and 1QFY28, to unlock ~Rs18bn and taking total InvIT investment  
to ~Rs33-35bn. Unlocked capital shall be utilised to reduce standalone debt (as 
the management targets net debt zero by FY28) and infusion of capital in HAM, 
renewables and MDO business. 
Management Commentaries: With 13 new order wins of Rs185bn in FY26 
(3 in Q4FY26), the OB reached a record ~Rs288bn (~4.1x TTM revenue).

  Earnings Concall – Key Takeaways 
Guidance  
◼ Standalone revenue is growth guided at ~30-40% y/y for FY27, aided by 
a healthy ~Rs280bn OB and strong execution visibility. EBITDA margin 
guidance

y for FY27, aided by 
a healthy ~Rs280bn OB and strong execution visibility. EBITDA margin 
guidance maintained at ~11 -12%, while targeted order inflows stand at 
~Rs100–120bn for FY27e. 
◼ The m anagement reiterated focus on becoming near net debt -free by 
FY28. Standalone debt currently stands at ~Rs18bn, against which the 
company holds ~Rs16bn of InvIT units. FY27 debt reduction guidance 
stands at ~Rs6 -8bn, aided by EPC cash generation, scaling mining 
operations and increasing InvIT distributions.  
◼ Capex discipline remains intact with focus on optimal utilisation of 
existing assets and selective capital allocation. Incremental investment 
required for transfer of remaining 11 HAM assets into InvIT stands at 
<Rs2bn, while asset monetisation and InvIT distributions continue to

M assets into InvIT stands at 
<Rs2bn, while asset monetisation and InvIT distributions continue to 
remain key balance sheet deleveraging levers.  
Bid Pipeline 
◼ DBL reported a record order inflow of ~Rs185bn in FY26, beating its 
original guidance. The current OB remains among the most diversified 
in the sector, while the active bid pipeline stands at >Rs800bn across 
roads, mining, transmission, water, urban infra and other infrastructure 
segments. 
◼ Infrastructure awarding activity remained relatively sluggish in FY26 due 
to elections, regulatory scrutiny and administrative delays. However, it 
remains optimistic on medium-to-long-term infrastructure opportunities, 
aided by continued government’s focus across roads, railways and other 
infra sectors.  
◼ Mining continues to scal

ued government’s focus across roads, railways and other 
infra sectors.  
◼ Mining continues to scale up as a key long -term earnings and cash flow 
driver. Consolidated coal production stood at ~28.7mmt in FY26, while 
the management aims scaling production to ~57m mt by FY29. Mining 
revenue is likely to rise from ~Rs16bn in FY26 to ~Rs25bn in FY27 and 
further to ~Rs40bn by FY29, aided by ramp -up at Siarmal and 
Pachhwara mines. 
Order Book and Order Inflows 
◼ With 13 new order wins of Rs185bn in FY26 (3 in Q4FY26), the OB 
reached a record ~Rs288bn (~4.1x TTM revenue) . It already achieved 
full-year order inflow guidance in FY26. The management indicated that 
~Rs800bn of bids are currently under evaluation across varied verticals.   
◼ FY26 order wins were largely EPC -led ( 11 EPC

rently under evaluation across varied verticals.   
◼ FY26 order wins were largely EPC -led ( 11 EPC and 2 HAM) and 
diversified across Rajasthan, Har yana, MP, Kerala, T N, Odisha, 
Karnataka, Bihar and Gujarat. Key large-ticket orders include: ~Rs49bn 
solar project under PM Kusum (MP), ~Rs34bn road project in Bihar, 
~Rs20bn irrigation HAM project in Rajasthan, Rs18.5bn  transmission 
project in Karnataka, and Rs17.5bn  (EPC value)  mining contract 
(NALCO, Odisha) 
◼ OB is diversified with roads constituting 19%, irrigation 16%, mining 
20%, tunnelling 6%, RE 18%, transmission 6% and others (optic fibres, 
special bridges, urban development , metro, water supply , petroleum & 
gas) 14%

MDO  
◼ Mining operations continued to scale up strongly in FY26, with Siarmal 
production reaching ~22.3 mmt and Pachhwara ~6.37 mmt, taking 
consolidated coal production to ~28.72 mmt for FY26 against original 
target of ~23mmt. 
◼ Its long-term target of scaling consolidated coal production to ~57m mt 
by FY29, positioning mining as a major long-duration earnings and cash-
flow driver. The management guided that mining revenue could rise from 
~Rs16bn in FY26 to ~Rs25/31/40bn in FY27/28/29e.  
◼ DBL recently added Pottangi Bauxite Mine from NALCO of ~Rs50bn 
spanning 25 years with option to extension for further 10 years. Brief scope of 
work includes extraction of annual

rs with option to extension for further 10 years. Brief scope of 
work includes extraction of annual 3.5mmt for 22 years, Installation of OLCC 
(conveyor) of 18.3km, construction of alternate road and water intake facility.   
◼ As per the management, temporary pressure on mining margin was due 
to delayed evacuation and unavailability of railway rakes at Siarmal, 
leading to inventory build-up at mine site. However, it expects margin to 
improve structurally, as operating leverage rises and coal handling plant 
becomes operational.  Rise in HSD cost  partially led to margin 
compression in FY26. 
HAM Monetisation and Alpha InvIT 
◼ The management reiterated that InvIT monetisation strategy remains on 
track, with seven HAM assets already transferred into Anantam 
Highways InvIT. The remai

remains on 
track, with seven HAM assets already transferred into Anantam 
Highways InvIT. The remaining 11 HAM assets are likely to be 
transferred gradually by Q1FY28, aligned with project completion/COD 
timelines. 
◼ Anantam Highways InvIT was listed in Q3FY26, with the management 
emphasising that the InvIT is intended to be a long -term annuity 
platform rather than a one-time monetisation event. 
◼ DBL currently holds ~Rs14bn worth of units in Anantam Highways 
InvIT along with ~Rs2bn in Shrem InvIT, taking total InvIT holdings 
on the balance sheet to nearly ~Rs16bn. 
◼ The remaining 11 HAM asset transfers are expected to require ~Rs1.7bn 
of incremental investment, while DBL expects to receive InvIT units 
valued at ~Rs18bn on transfer, implying substantial equity value creation

to receive InvIT units 
valued at ~Rs18bn on transfer, implying substantial equity value creation 
and balance-sheet strengthening. Post completion of all 18 HAM asset 
transfers, total InvIT unit value is expected to rise to ~Rs30-33bn. 
◼ Currently, the management does not intend to monetise the InvIT units, 
as the broader strategy is to build a long -duration distribution platform 
generating predictable cash flows over the next 15 -20 years. InvIT 
distribution, EPC cash generation and mining cash flows are likely to 
support deleveraging and the targeted near net debt-free balance sheet by 
FY28e. 
Debt 
◼ Net debt (standalone) stood at ~Rs18.8bn as of Q4 vs.  Rs21bn as of Q3.  
◼ For FY27, the management guided for debt reduction of ~Rs6 -8bn. It 
also highlighted that debt has alr

FY27, the management guided for debt reduction of ~Rs6 -8bn. It 
also highlighted that debt has already reduced by ~Rs2.5 -3bn q/q. The 
management reiterated that DBL aims to be near net debt-free by FY28e.

◼ The management clarified that the strategy is to minimise its own BS 
equity commitment in transmission and RE SPVs. Around 85% of total 
equity requirement is likely to be funded by external investors directly at 
SPV level, while DBL itself would contribute only ~15% equity. 
◼ Total equity requirement for these projects is ~Rs16bn (~Rs12bn in solar 
and ~Rs4bn in transmission). However, DBL’s own contribution would 
remain l

16bn (~Rs12bn in solar 
and ~Rs4bn in transmission). However, DBL’s own contribution would 
remain limited (~15%) due to the planned investor participation 
structure. 
◼ The broader objective behind this structure is to preserve FCF, reduce 
standalone debt and achieve near net debt-free BS by FY28.

  Outlook and Valuation 
Moderate execution in FY26 was due to lagged impact of lean OB at the 
beginning of the year. However, DBL saw string of awards post Q1FY26 
with record inflow of ~Rs185bn and a record OB of ~Rs288bn. We factor 
in the lead time to achieve desired execution of newly added orders  and 
expect ramping up with desired execution levels in FY27 . Thu

execution of newly added orders  and 
expect ramping up with desired execution levels in FY27 . Thus, we increase 
our revenue estimate marginally by ~3.2/1.5% for FY27/28e effectively 
translating to revenue CAGR of ~20% over FY26-28e. Operational 
efficiency is expected to set in partially off-setting rise in input cost, marginally 
increasing EBITDA margin by ~13/9bps in FY27/28e   
Considering the diversified OB with recent foray into RE and transmission, 
progress in MDO and InvIT listing, and strong opportunity pipeline , w e 
maintain HOLD rating on the stock with a revised SOTP-based TP of Rs596 
(from Rs572 earlier) with the core-EPC business rolled forward and valuing 
it at 8x FY28e EPS.
